title.full: When someone close to you dies

journeys.summary: What has to happen in the first days, what can wait a few weeks, and what is settled months later.

example_phrasings: what do I do when someone dies

what to do after a death in Singapore
my wife passed on, how do I handle her CPF and the flat

stages.name: Get the death certificate
stages.note: A doctor certifies the death and it is registered for you. The certificate is downloaded, not collected.
stages.done_when: You have the digital death certificate on your phone or printed.

stages.name: Arrange the funeral
stages.note: The funeral director does most of this. Cremation and burial slots are booked through them.
stages.done_when: The funeral, cremation or burial is arranged and a date is set.

stages.name: Hand back the NRIC
stages.note: One small thing that is easy to forget in the first week.
stages.done_when: The NRIC has been returned, or you have been told you need not.

stages.name: Claim the CPF savings
stages.note: If they made a nomination, CPF pays the nominees. If they did not, the Public Trustee handles it.
stages.done_when: The CPF savings have been paid out, or the Public Trustee has your application.

stages.name: Claim the funeral costs back
stages.note: Money already spent on the funeral can be reimbursed out of what they left.
stages.done_when: The claim for funeral expenses has been sent with the receipts.

stages.name: Find and claim what they held
stages.note: Banks will not talk to you without the certificate, and often not without a grant.
stages.done_when: You know what accounts and shares there are, and have claimed them.

stages.name: Settle the estate
stages.note: With a will, this is probate. Without one, it is Letters of Administration. Either takes months.
stages.done_when: The grant has been issued and what they left has been distributed.

journeys.concludes_when: The estate is distributed, the accounts are closed, and nothing is left outstanding in their name.
